unit.why: A short narrative: the disciple Meir Leib weeps in Lublin over the death of the Holy Jew, and the Seer of Lublin summons him and comforts him.

stories.start_quote: סיפר כי היה בלובלין אז כשנתוודע
stories.summary_en: When news came of the Holy Jew's death, Meir Leib wept so bitterly in Lublin that he left town to hide it; the Seer of Lublin summoned him, embraced him, admitted he too had rolled in the dust weeping, and urged him to stop, since 'our God lives forever.'

tags.why: Excessive grief and weeping is the problem the Seer addresses.

quotes: עד שהיה ירא לבכות כ״כ בפני אנשים
tags.why: He fears weeping before the hasidim.
The death of the Holy Jew is the triggering event, reported rather than depicted.

quotes: ומיד חיבק אותו ואמר לו מאיר לעב
tags.why: The Seer's tender care for his disciple is central.

quotes: בפני אנשים החסידים שמה שיאמרו כי הלא מרן הק' מלובלין הוא עמנו
tags.why: He worries what the Lublin hasidim would say.
The story is set at the Seer's court in Lublin.
Framed as the subject's own recounted memory.

quotes: כי ההק׳ היהודי ז״ל איננו, אבל אלהיינו הוא חי וקיים לעד
tags.why: Reflection on the place of the tsaddik versus God after a tsaddik's death.
